010.description: The United States as a whole. The top of the census geographic hierarchy.

020.description: One of the four Census regions (Northeast, Midwest, South, West) that group states for statistical reporting.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

030.description: One of the nine Census divisions that subdivide the four Census regions into groups of states.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

040.description: A U.S. state or state-equivalent such as the District of Columbia or Puerto Rico.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

050.description: A county or county-equivalent, the primary legal subdivision of a state.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

060.description: A county subdivision, which in Ohio are townships and the cities and villages that have separated from them. Nests within a county.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

070.description: The part of a county subdivision that is either within a given place or outside all places (the remainder), split by county. Used to separate townships from the cities and villages that overlap them.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

100.description: A census block, the smallest unit of census geography, bounded by visible features such as streets and streams and by legal boundaries. Nests within a block group.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

140.description: A census tract, a small, relatively stable statistical subdivision of a county that typically holds 1,200 to 8,000 people. Nests within a county.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

150.description: A block group, a cluster of census blocks within a tract that typically holds 600 to 3,000 people. The smallest geography for most American Community Survey estimates.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

155.description: The portion of a place that falls within a given county. Places that cross county lines are split into one part per county.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

160.description: A place, meaning an incorporated city or village or a census designated place (CDP). Places can cross county lines.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

310.description: A metropolitan or micropolitan statistical area (core-based statistical area), made up of one or more counties around an urban core plus adjacent counties with strong commuting ties.

M6.description: OMB Bulletin No. 20-01 delineations. Used in 2020 Census data products.

400.description: An urban area, a densely settled territory delineated by the Census Bureau from housing and population density, independent of political boundaries.

C1.description: 2010 Census urban-rural classification. 2020 ACS tabulations use this code.

C2.description: 2020 Census urban-rural classification. Used in 2020 Census tabulations.

500.description: A district from which a member of the U.S. House of Representatives is elected. Redrawn after each decennial census.

860.description: A ZIP code tabulation area, the Census Bureau's generalized areal representation of a five-digit USPS ZIP code, built from census blocks.

950.description: An elementary school district, which serves only the lower grades and is overlaid by a secondary school district.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

960.description: A secondary school district, which serves only the upper grades and overlays one or more elementary school districts.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

970.description: A unified school district, which serves all grade levels. Most Ohio school districts are unified.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

M01.description: A MORPC region made by combining whole counties, such as the 15-county MORPC region. Consolidates the county-based regions that currently each have their own sumlevel.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

M02.description: A MORPC region made by combining jurisdiction county parts, for regions whose boundaries follow municipal or township lines rather than county lines.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

M10.description: A jurisdiction, the closest representation of municipal and political jurisdictions: whole cities and villages plus the township remainders outside them.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

M11.description: A jurisdiction county part, meaning a jurisdiction split by county so that a city or village crossing a county line is represented once per county.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

M30.description: A solid waste (refuse) management district, the county or multi-county district responsible for solid waste planning in Ohio.

M31.description: A library district, the service area of a public library system.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

M32.description: A campus, the boundary of a college, university, or similar institutional campus.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

M40.description: A cell in a regular one-mile grid covering the region, used to summarize data independently of administrative boundaries.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.

M41.description: A cell in a regular quarter-mile grid, made by dividing each one-mile grid cell into sixteen.

00.description: Default: no geographic variant specified. Boundaries are updated annually, so the vintage is the data year.
